subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the food test, what colour does Benedict's solution turn when heated with a reducing sugar?
questions.explain: Benedict's solution turns from blue to brick-red/orange when a reducing sugar is present.

questions.q: In the menstrual cycle, which hormone maintains the uterus lining in the second half of the cycle?
questions.explain: Progesterone maintains the thickened uterus lining; when its level falls, the lining breaks down and menstruation occurs.

questions.q: Why does the large intestine play a role at the end of digestion?
options: It absorbs amino acids into the blood
It absorbs water from undigested food to form faeces
questions.explain: The large intestine absorbs water, leaving solid faeces to be egested.

questions.q: Which hormone lowers blood glucose concentration when it rises too high?
questions.explain: Insulin, released by the pancreas, causes cells to take up glucose and the liver to store it as glycogen, lowering blood glucose.

questions.q: Adrenaline, released in a frightening situation, prepares the body for 'fight or flight' by:
options: Increasing heart rate and boosting glucose supply to muscles
Causing the body to fall asleep
questions.explain: Adrenaline increases heart rate and raises blood glucose, supplying muscles with more oxygen and energy.

questions.q: Which enzyme breaks down starch into sugars?
questions.explain: Amylase is a carbohydrase that digests starch into simple sugars such as maltose.

questions.q: Hormones are transported around the body in the:
questions.explain: Hormones are chemical messengers secreted by glands and carried in the blood to target organs.

questions.q: During filtration in the kidney, which substance is NOT normally found in the filtrate of a healthy person?
questions.explain: Large proteins and blood cells are too big to be filtered, so they stay in the blood; glucose is filtered but reabsorbed.

questions.q: What is homeostasis?
options: The breakdown of glucose for energy
The maintenance of a constant internal environment
questions.explain: Homeostasis is the regulation of internal conditions, such as temperature and blood glucose, within set limits.

questions.q: Compared with a conscious response, a spinal reflex is:
options: The same speed but uses more neurones
Slower and decided by the brain
Faster because it bypasses conscious brain processing
questions.explain: Reflexes are faster than conscious responses because they do not pass through the conscious brain.

questions.q: In the menstrual cycle, a surge of which hormone triggers ovulation?
questions.explain: A surge in LH at around day 14 stimulates the release of an egg (ovulation).

questions.q: In dim light, the pupil reflex causes the:
options: Pupil to get larger to let more light in
questions.explain: In dim light radial muscles contract and the pupil widens to let more light reach the retina.

questions.q: Why does breaking large food molecules into smaller ones help the body?
options: Small soluble molecules can be absorbed across the gut wall into the blood
questions.explain: Digestion makes molecules small and soluble enough to be absorbed into the bloodstream.

questions.q: Which part of the eye changes shape to focus light on the retina?
questions.explain: The lens changes shape (accommodation) to focus light from near or distant objects onto the retina.

questions.q: Which nutrient is the body's main source of energy?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates are the primary energy source in a balanced diet.

questions.q: In the reflex arc, what is the 'effector'?
options: The receptor that detects the stimulus
A muscle or gland that produces the response
The relay neurone in the spinal cord
questions.explain: An effector is a muscle or gland that carries out the response, such as a muscle contracting.

questions.q: Which hormone causes the lining of the uterus to thicken during the menstrual cycle?
questions.explain: Oestrogen, produced by the ovaries, causes the uterus lining to build up ready for a possible pregnancy.

questions.q: Type 2 diabetes is associated with:
options: A complete lack of a pancreas
Too much insulin being produced from birth
The body's cells no longer responding properly to insulin
questions.explain: In Type 2 diabetes cells stop responding to insulin; it is linked to obesity and often controlled by diet and exercise.

questions.q: On a hot day, a person sweats a lot and becomes dehydrated. How does the body respond to conserve water?
options: More ADH is released, so the kidneys reabsorb more water
questions.explain: When dehydrated, more ADH is released, making kidney tubules reabsorb more water, producing less, more concentrated urine.

questions.q: A plant shoot grows towards light. This response is called:
questions.explain: Growth towards light is positive phototropism, controlled by the hormone auxin.

questions.q: What is the main role of the stomach in digestion?
options: Produces hydrochloric acid and protease to begin protein digestion
questions.explain: The stomach secretes hydrochloric acid and the protease pepsin to start digesting protein.

questions.q: What does a receptor in the nervous system do?
options: Detects a stimulus such as light, heat or pressure
questions.explain: Receptors detect stimuli (changes in the environment) and convert them into electrical impulses.
